subject: Outdoor Dining Ordinance Updates
overview: The committee reviewed a proposal from the Office of Economic Development to establish a permanent outdoor dining ordinance as state emergency orders expire. Members discussed design standards, accessibility, and furniture maintenance, requesting a revised draft that incorporates specific safety and aesthetic requirements.

items.title: Outdoor Dining Ordinance Proposal
items.summary: Director of Economic Development Victor Schrader presented a plan to streamline outdoor dining permits through the building department and establish consistent safety, ADA, and seasonal guidelines.

items.title: Maintenance and Design Standards
items.summary: Councilors proposed requirements for locking furniture and removing trash nightly, and they discussed implementing minimum aesthetic standards for barriers and seating areas.

items.title: Accessibility and Parklet Construction
items.summary: The committee deliberated on ADA compliance, with a specific focus on requiring that in-street parklet platforms be built level with the curb to improve accessibility.

items.title: Animal Policy and Operations
items.summary: The proposal included a new provision allowing restaurants the option to permit dogs in outdoor dining areas, provided they meet health and control requirements.

items.title: Motions and Referral
items.summary: Approved motions requiring furniture to be locked, trash removed nightly, and minimum design standards; a second motion passed requesting recommendations for curb-level parklet construction. The matter was kept in committee pending a revised ordinance draft.
